items.title: Amazon Acquires DuckLabs and Integrates DuckDB in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
items.summary: Amazon has acquired DuckLabs, the company behind the analytical database DuckDB. Co-founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt will continue to lead the team under AWS. The acquisition aims to enhance the development and reach of DuckDB while maintaining its open-source status. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL gets its first DuckDB-powered feature following the acquisition. By Gianmarco Nalin

items.title: Uber Automates Dependency Analysis Across Its Service Mesh
items.summary: Uber has developed an automated dependency analysis system that uses RPC middleware and production metrics to correlate caller and downstream failures. The approach classifies dependencies as fail-close, fail-open, or unknown and addresses limitations of sampled distributed tracing for rare failures across Uber’s large service mesh. By Leela Kumili

items.title: Presentation: Exploding GPUs
items.summary: Andrew Martin discusses why AI security is fundamentally tied to Kubernetes security. He shares insights into the evolving AI threat landscape, covering non-deterministic agent behavior, GPU supply chain vulnerabilities, shared compute risks, and practical defense strategies - from prompt firewalling to agentic identity - to help secure cloud-native AI workloads in production environments. By Andrew Martin

items.title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
items.summary: AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution. Both projects address different aspects of building agents that use tools, execute code, and interact with external systems. By Daniel Dominguez

items.title: Microsoft Commits Maia to Multi-Gigawatt Inference, and Its Efficiency Metric Draws Questions
items.summary: Microsoft will scale its Maia accelerator family to multi-gigawatt deployments from 2027, making it the primary inference system for its own products. Maia 300 collapses scale-up and scale-out onto one Ethernet fabric and moves KV state between prefill and decode workers without leaving it. Practitioners have questioned the tokens-per-watt claim that leads the announcement. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

items.title: Länderübergreifende Recherche: Palantirs Geschäfte in Europa
items.summary: Palantir steht in Europa unter Druck. – Alle Rechte vorbehalten: Rosa Snijders / Follow The Money Software von Palantir findet sich bei europäischen Streitkräften, bei Polizeien und im Gesundheitssystem. Aber viele Länder suchen nach Alternativen, sie sorgen sich um Abhängigkeiten, Sicherheit und Demokratie. Ein Recherche-Team hat untersucht, wo der Tech-Konzern in Europa Verträge mit Regierungen hat.

items.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
items.summary: Zod is a TypeScript-focused schema validation library that recently released versions 4.5 and 4.6. Key updates include schema compilation for faster data parsing, significant memory usage reductions, and new validation features. The library supports efficient validation processes and remains popular in the JavaScript ecosystem, achieving millions of downloads weekly. By Daniel Curtis

items.title: Helidon 27 Introduces Restructured Programming Models and New Messaging and Data Modules
items.summary: The release of Helidon 27 is the first release that follows the Oracle Tip & Tail Model of Library Development by which the Tip adopts the latest Java technology while the Tail provides a more stable and secure baseline. Concurrent with the release of JDK 27, new features in Helidon 27 include: an introduction to new major modules, Helidon Messaging and Helidon Data JDBC. By Michael Redlich
